description.narrative: The objective of the Youth Employment Transformation Initiative Project in Nepal is to improve employment services and labor market outcomes, especially for youth. This project has three components. Component 1: Strengthening of employment promotion systems and services. The objective is to support the Government of Nepal (GoN) in building a platform for a systematic approach to provision of employment promotion services. Subcomponent 1a: Increasing access to employment opportunities. This subcomponent will support effective and systematic provision of employment promotion and unemployment support services by strengthening the Employment Service Center (ESC) in the Local Levels (LL) to deliver their functions. Subcomponent 1b: Developing a holistic National Employment Management Information System (NEMIS). This subcomponent will support development of a holistic NEMIS for the efficient and effective functioning of employment promotion services. Component 2: Improving labor market outcomes of the vulnerable. This component aims to support skills and productivity enhancement for poor and vulnerable job seekers through temporary employment with on-the-job training and life-skills training, aligned to the Prime Minister's Employment Program (PMEP). Component 3: Project management, monitoring and evaluation, and capacity building. This component will support (a) the establishment and maintenance of effective implementation and coordination arrangements at the federal, provincial and local levels; (b) the setup of an Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) mechanism to track the progress (spot checks, beneficiary feedback mechanisms, a grievance redress system, and policy reviews) and conduct evaluations (including a robust impact evaluation); (c) conducting regular sector policy reviews; and (d) capacity-building programs for project implementation, management, Prime Minister's Employment Program (PMEP) service delivery, and cross-component activities.
To improve employment services and labor market outcomes, especially for youth.

condition.narrative: For Emergency Expenditures under Component 5 of the Project, unless the Recipient has determined that an Eligible Crisis orEmergency has occurred, has furnished to the Association a request to include said activities in the CERC Part in order to respondto said Eligible Crisis or Emergency, and the Association has agreed with such determination, accepted said request and notifiedthe Recipient.
No later than two (2) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall assign at least two (2) finance officers to the PMU withqualifications and terms of reference acceptable to the Association

Not later than four (4) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall hire a procurement consultant with qualifications andterms of reference acceptable to the Association to support the PMU in carrying out Project procurement.

Not later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall hire at least one administrative support staff for eachESC with qualifications and terms of reference acceptable to the Association

The Recipient shall appoint a Provincial Project Coordinator in each of the seven Provincial Governments, who will be the UnderSecretary of the respective MoSD and shall carry out monitoring and evaluation activities and coordinate between the FederalGovernment, the Provincial Governments and the LLs

The Recipient shall establish and thereafter maintain throughout the period of implementation of the Project not later than three(3) months after the Effective Date, a Project Technical Committee to provide technical guidance to the Project consisting ofofficials and technical experts of relevant ministries/agencies as well as the private sector

The Recipient shall establish and thereafter maintain throughout the period of implementation of the Project not later than two (2)months after the Effective Date, a Project Management Unit, which will oversee the overall Project implementation, manage theday-to-day operations, including procurement, financial management, safeguards and monitoring and evaluation, and provide guidance,technical support and training to LLs, and will prepare and consolidate financial and implementation reports. The PMU shall be ledby a National Project Director and staffed with professionals, all of whom shall have qualifications, experience and terms ofreference satisfactory to the Association

The Recipient shall establish and thereafter maintain throughout the period of implementation of the Project not later than two (2)months after the Effective Date, an Inter-Ministerial Project Steering Committee with composition and terms of referencesatisfactory to the Association

The Recipient, through appropriate procedures and transaction mechanisms with LLs, shall ensure that the LLs, with the support ofthe ESCs, are responsible for management, and basic functions of financial management, procurement and safeguards associated withtheir respective activities under the Project. To that end, the Recipient shall: (a) include in the Operating Guidelines,appropriate provisions to ensure that the terms of this Agreement and the POM are passed down to all LLs as special conditions fortheir respective Conditional Grants; and (b) ensure that all LLs receive all relevant documents describing in detail theresponsibilities of all LLs in relation to the implementation of their respective activities under the Project in accordance withthis Agreement.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of social safety net programs

comment.narrative: This does not include the CERC beneficiaires, who are captured under the CERC intermediate indicator.

title.narrative: Number of beneficiaries that completed on-the-job and life skills training

comment.narrative: The project trained 13,379 beneficiaries across 345 LLs (target 21,000) , with implementation constrained by procurement delays. The training lasted 50 days and included a life skills package. Courses focused on five trades (road repair and maintenance, electrical repairs, masonry, carpentry, and plumbing), to align with TEPs planned at LLs, while life skills training complemented technical modules to enhance employability. The modules were adapted from the existing curriculum to suit the target beneficiaries' education level.

title.narrative: Number of workdays created through temporary employment programs

comment.narrative: In total, 15.2 million workdays were generated across 753 LLs, exceeding the planned 12.1 million.

title.narrative: Number of people (disaggregated by gender and age group) supported by the project who take up a training, temporary work, or employment opportunity within one year of registration

comment.narrative: The project achieved its PDO indicators for short-term employment and youth inclusion. YETI reached 185,968 beneficiaries (99 percent of target); youth participation was 64 percent, and women accounted for over 53 percent of beneficiaries.

title.narrative: Number of Employment Service Centers (ESCs) which are established and functional

comment.narrative: A total of 753 ESCs, one in each LL, were established, and 739 were reported as functional at closing. The four functions referred to are (a) register, profile, and counsel job seekers and the unemployed; (b) provide referral services; (c) coordinate provision of temporary employment; and (d) provide inputs into NEMIS and generate reports based on NEMIS data. Out of the total, 739 ESCs were able to carry out three essential functions.For each of the four functions, the number of ESCs able to perform the specific function varied between 739 and 749. In the last one year, facilitation for labor permits for foreign employment and referrals and counseling for families of migrant workers was also provided.

title.narrative: Number of Local Levels trained on managing and implementation of temporary employment programs

comment.narrative: At least one LL staff in each LL was trained regularly on temporary employment guidelines, implementation, and monitoring.

title.narrative: Number of Local Levels where ESC personnel is trained on delivery of ESC functions

comment.narrative: Staff capacities were strengthened through regular induction and refresher training on EMIS and the Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF). The 30 model ESCs received enhanced training, allowing them to pilot expanded service functions such as job matching, employer outreach, labor permit facilitation, and market-oriented vocational training.

title.narrative: Number of Local Levels where gender sensitive outreach campaign has been conducted

comment.narrative: The gender-sensitive outreach campaign was conducted across all 753 local levels. Gender considerations were mainstreamed across awareness and outreach.

title.narrative: Percentage of grievances registered related to the delivery of the project which are addressed as per the agreed service standard

comment.narrative: 33 grievances were logged, of which 27 were addressed (82%), within the required timeframe.

title.narrative: Percentage of project beneficiaries satisfied with the employment services received (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: The satisfaction survey conducted in June 2024 reported 99.5 percent overall satisfaction, with wages primarily used to meet household needs such as food, education, and basic health expenditures.

title.narrative: Establishment of core functions of a National Employment Management Information System

baseline.value: Jobs portal exist and temporary employment module of NEMIS designing underway

target.value: Core functions of National Employment Managment Information System are established.

comment.narrative: A national employment information system with the expected functionalities has been established, even though the original procurement for NEMIS was not completed. The project did not directly develop the system due to repeated procurement delays, but the PDO target was achieved through the Government's adoption and scale-up of the Shramsansar platform.

title.narrative: Additional people participating in temporary employment during COVID pandemic

comment.narrative: 43,834 were reached through the activation of the CERC, which temporarily expanded the public works program during the COVID-19 pandemic . Restructuring (2024) reallocated unspent CERC funds to finance additional temporary employment (safety net beneficiaries). The 2024 restructuring raised the PDO target from 167,000 to 188,000 beneficiaries to account for the increase, but the COVID target was not revised downward, which explains the apparent shortfall against the original indicator's target.
